queries: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM rating_counts) SELECT AVG(rc.cnt) AS avg_count_above_average, AVG(rc.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_overall_average FROM rating_counts rc CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE rc.cnt > o.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: A rental transaction is one row in rental. Each row is linked to a film through rental.inventory_id -> inventory.film_id -> film.rating.

The overall average is the unweighted mean of the 5 per-rating counts, not the mean per film. The output is the mean count of the above-average ratings and the mean of (count - overall average) for those same ratings.

assumptions.assumption: The overall average count is the unweighted mean of the per-rating rental counts (one value per rating), not rentals per film or per copy.
Every rental row counts as one rental transaction, whether or not it was returned or has a payment.

assumptions.assumption: The 'average count across all ratings' is the mean of the per-rating rental counts (one value per rating, 5 ratings), not an average per film or per rental.
Each rental is one rental transaction (rows in the rental table), and every rental maps to exactly one film via inventory, so an inner join loses no rentals.
